methods.label: Screen dimensions and proportional parts
methods.explanation:
The screen's aspect ratio lets us express both dimensions using one scale factor. Let its width be \(4t\) inches and its height be \(3t\) inches, where \(t>0\). The diagonal forms a right triangle with these sides, so the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
27^2=(4t)^2+(3t)^2=25t^2.
\]
Thus \(5t=27\), giving \(t=27/5\).

[Figure 1](figures/2008_AMC_10A_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

The movie occupies the full width \(4t\). Its \(2:1\) aspect ratio therefore makes its height \(2t\). The two equal strips together occupy the remaining height \(3t-2t=t\), so each strip has height
\[
\frac{t}{2}=\frac{27}{10}=\boxed{2.7}\text{ inches}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\mathrm{D}}\).
